content:
/poll I noticed we have two types of braces for both Hoare triples and WP's: the ASCII ones from normal Iris, and the fancy unicode ones. Unfortunately, the unicode syntax clashes with Std.do, so you can't open both notations in the same file. I'd propose we remove the fancy unicode braces and just stick to the ASCII ones unless anyone has strong opinions. What do you think?
I don't care / remove unicode
I want to keep the unicode braces

Actually, I purposefuly chose the unicode syntax because it was just like Std.Do's syntax, thinking that it would be nice to have the same syntax for both. I guess I didn't realize that this is actually a problem since it generates ambiguity, my bad!

Maybe I could achieve what I originally wanted by using the iprop trick to give a different interpretation to Hoare triples? This seems complicated though. In any case, all in on simply removing the unicode interpretation, I think the ASCII notation is also just clearer to use

Without much further context, it seems a little worrying to have two very similar syntaxes being disambiguated just by unicode vs non-unicode? Would it be clear from context which of the two is meant when both are used intermingled?

Actually, I imagine that the Iris Hoare triples are already different from Std.Do's in that I don't imagine that they specify postconditions in the say way as we do. In Iris, we have {{ x y, RET (pat x y); postcond }} for the postcondition part, and from what I remember Std.Do has something like ⦃ ⇓ x y => postcond ⦄
In that case, is there an MWE where both scopes being opened causes an error? I'd be curious to have a look.

I tried reproducing it this morning and was not able to--I was trying a bunch of stuff out yesterday mixing the two frameworks so this might have been inaccurate. Either way, I think having duplicate notation is not good so I will make a PR deleting it.
